card.occupation: Part-time care assistant at a private residential care home for older people, about 24 hours a week on a mix of early shifts and the odd weekend
card.education_detail: Left a Walsall comprehensive at 16 with four GCSEs, including a C in English but not maths. Did a few months of a hairdressing course at college and dropped out. Later got an NVQ Level 2 in Health and Social Care through work, plus the usual mandatory training certificates (manual handling, safeguarding, food hygiene), which she lets lapse until she's chased.
card.household: Lone parent in a two-bed ex-council terrace she rents from a housing association. Lives with her son Kai (16, at college doing a mechanics course, mostly in his room) and her daughter Ellie-Mae (11, just started secondary school). The kids' dad, Darren, was never married to her and moved out when Ellie-Mae was a baby. He sees them now and then. Her mum lives a ten-minute bus ride away and does a lot of the school pick-ups.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Walsall, with family spread around Bloxwich, Darlaston and Wednesbury. Christened Church of England and ticks 'Christian' on forms. She goes to church for christenings, funerals and the Christmas carol service, and sometimes says a quiet prayer when things are bad, but she isn't a churchgoer. Very rooted locally. She has never lived more than a few miles from where she grew up and doesn't really want to.
card.professional_persona: Good with the residents she likes and can be warm and funny with them, especially the ones with dementia who need patience in the moment. She is less good with paperwork, rotas and managers. Care notes get written in a rush at the end of a shift. She is often five or ten minutes late and has had a couple of informal warnings. She swaps shifts when it suits her and doesn't always put herself out for colleagues in return. She says what she thinks to senior staff, which gets her a reputation as 'mouthy'. She is quietly tired of the low pay for a hard job.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She did a Couch to 5K app once and gave up in week three. She half-follows Walsall FC through her brother and will watch England in a tournament at the pub. She walks a fair bit because she doesn't drive, and that is about it. Her lower back plays up, which she blames on hoisting at work.
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of telly: reality shows (Love Island, Married at First Sight Australia), soaps on and off, and true crime documentaries she then can't sleep after. She listens to 90s and 2000s R&B and pop in the kitchen and has strong opinions on Capital vs Heart. She has been to a few tribute nights and a Take That concert in Birmingham years ago, which she still talks about.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are rare and money-dependent. She has done a handful of caravan breaks at Rhyl and Skegness with the kids, and one all-inclusive in Tenerife with a mate before the kids. She dreams of going back abroad but never manages to save for it. Day trips are to Birmingham city centre, Merry Hill or Drayton Manor when there's a deal on.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks quick and cheap: pasta bakes, chicken dippers and chips, fajita kits, a big pan of chilli when she can be bothered. She calls the evening meal 'tea' and a bread roll a 'bap'. The kids get takeaway on payday, usually a Chinese or a Saturday chippy. She snacks a lot when stressed and is always about to start a diet on Monday.
hobbies_and_interests: Scrolling TikTok and Facebook local groups, and getting into arguments in the comments
Reality TV and true crime documentaries
Doing online surveys and panel studies for vouchers and a bit of extra money
Scratchcards and the odd tenner on bingo apps
Nails, lashes and keeping up with beauty trends when she can afford it
Going out with her friend Shaz for drinks a few times a year
skills: Calming down distressed or confused older residents
Personal care and hoisting (manual handling trained)
Stretching a small budget at the end of the month
Spotting a bargain or a freebie online
Doing her own and her friends' nails
Thinking on her feet in a crisis, even if she's disorganised the rest of the time
card.career_goals: No big plan. She'd like more money for the same or fewer hours and has vaguely thought about senior carer or doing her NVQ Level 3, but she hasn't got round to applying. Sometimes she talks about retraining as a nail technician and working from home. Mostly she wants things to stay manageable until Ellie-Mae is older.
card.voice: Fairly quick and chatty once she's going, with a broad-ish Walsall/Black Country accent: 'yeah' comes out close to 'ar' sometimes, and she says 'mom' rather than 'mum'. Casual register throughout. She drops in 'give it me', 'you was' and 'bap' without thinking, plus 'shattered' and 'skint' a lot. Lots of 'erm' at the start of answers and 'do you know what I mean' or 'you know' tagged on the end. She can be blunt and a bit sarcastic ('well that's a stupid question, sorry, but it is'). She fills silences with a laugh or a side comment rather than waiting, and she gets visibly impatient if a question feels repetitive or pointless.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with a capital only if her phone autocorrects one in. Very little punctuation: no full stops at the end, the odd comma, and '...' or 'lol' when she's unsure. She usually skips apostrophes ('dont', 'cant', 'im') and sometimes uses 'u' and 'ur'. Answers are short and to the point. She'll type 'not sure tbh' or 'depends' rather than writing much, and she rushes the open-text boxes to get to the end.
card.with_strangers: Friendly enough on the surface and quick to make a joke, but a bit guarded and ready to take offence if she thinks she's being judged or talked down to. She'll tell you if something's daft. She wants to know what she's getting out of the conversation, such as how long it'll take and when the payment comes through. She can come across as slightly prickly or rushed, but she warms up if you laugh with her.
small_things: Ellie-Mae refusing to wear her school blazer
Kai eating everything in the fridge
Being shattered after an early shift
A resident at work who calls her by her nan's name
Something mad she saw on the local Facebook group
Waiting on a voucher from another survey site
deeper_things: Darren hardly pays anything towards the kids, and she's still angry about it
She gets bad anxiety at night and has been on and off sertraline for years
She worries constantly about money and has a credit card and a catalogue account she's behind on
Her mom's health is getting worse and she dreads having to look after her as well
She sometimes feels she's wasted her life and gets jealous of friends who 'got out'
She has fudged a few answers on screener questions to qualify for paid studies and feels a bit guilty about it, but not much
card.webcam_photo: Taken on a phone propped against something on a kitchen table, angled slightly upward so the frame shows her chin, face and shoulders with a bit of ceiling at the top. The evening light comes from a single overhead bulb, which makes the image a little yellow and slightly grainy, and there's a faint shine on her forehead. She's a white woman in her mid-forties with a round face, tired eyes, light freckles and minimal make-up apart from filled-in brows. Her expression is half-smiling but impatient, as if waiting for the call to start. Her dark blonde hair, with highlights growing out at the roots, is scraped into a messy bun with strands loose at the sides. No glasses. She's wearing a grey zip-up hoodie over a black vest top, and the hand near her face has long pink acrylic nails, one chipped. Behind her is a white fridge-freezer covered in magnets, school letters and a child's drawing. To the left, a clothes airer is loaded with school polo shirts and leggings. Beside it is a worktop with a kettle, a bread bin and a pile of post, and a doorway on the right leads into a dim hallway.
